n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, trend accuracy (the fraction of participants that predicted the correct trend in the data) in round 3 in the Partisan priming treatment is 49.50% (se = 2.6%, n = 28), while it is 50.4% (se = 2.8%, n = 28) in the No Partisan Cues treatment. This difference in trend accuracy between conditions was tested using a Mann- Whitney-U test with each network aggregated into one observation and 28 aggregated observations per treatment (z = 0.254, p = 0.799; n = 56). In the replication experiment, the sum of ranks is larger in the Partisan Priming treatment (∑r = 813.5) than in the No Partisan Cues treatment (∑r = 782.5), i.e., the effect points in the opposite direction of the original study. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = –0.068 (95% CI [–0.592, 0.456]).
